note: N-007. `set(count, flag)` names its parameter like the mutable property `count` and reads it inside an `if` arm: `if (flag) { assert(count == 5n); } this.count = count;`. Before N-007 the TS, Go, Rust, Zig and Ruby tiers lowered the arm in a fresh context that lost the parameter's reserved `__param_count` slot mapping, so the arm read the deserialized on-chain state (OP_DUP of count) instead of the witness argument: with state 5, set(7, true) was ACCEPTED. Expected verdicts are derived by hand from the source.
